title: Cap. 1 subject: bare election vs means — Davenant's judgment
pass_a_gloss: But that I may in a few words set forth what is of my judgment in this matter. First, if through Predestination someone understands sole designation unto the end of glory (just as many understand from the more ancient Scholastics) and through Reprobation the sole negation of this act, or the decree itself of passing by and not electing, I think it is not necessary that we suppose sin to have been foreseen in the subject thus predestined or reprobated, as something preceding. This is the reason; Because in the acts of the Divine mind and will one is not really prior to another, but this whole priority and posteriority is taken from the mutual dependence of the things: where therefore there is no dependence of causality among the things themselves, no consideration of priority or posteriority ought or can be in the Divine decrees which turn about the same. But now sin holds itself altogether impertinently toward the act of Divine election or non election: for it is not the reason of the act either of this or of that (as all confess) nor is it such a qualification of the subject without which these acts cannot fall upon the subject, as rationality is; which by the example of the Angels was demonstrated before. Since therefore sin is neither the cause why someone is elected unto glory, or permitted to fail from glory, nor a disposition of the subject necessary either unto this act or unto that, he speaks improperly who says this decree of electing or not electing is prior in the Divine mind to the foresight of sin; he also speaks improperly who says the foresight of sin was prior to this decree, since among independent things neither priority nor posteriority is to be placed, whether in the mind or in the will of God. And from this you can gather that those who try by I know not what horrendous consequences to defile the opinion of those who consider the decree of election and passing by without foresight of sin, are tying ropes from sand.
pass_b_english: My judgment in brief. First: if by Predestination you mean bare designation to the end of glory (as many older Scholastics do), and by Reprobation only the negation of that act — the decree to pass by and not elect — I do not think foresight of sin must be supposed as something prior in the subject so predestined or reprobated. Why? In God's mind and will no act is really prior to another; all before-and-after is taken from the mutual dependence of the things themselves. Where the things have no causal dependence, Divine decrees about them admit no before or after. Sin is altogether beside the point for the act of Divine election or non-election. It is not the reason of either act (all confess that), nor a qualification of the subject without which those acts cannot fall — as rationality is; the angels already showed that. Since sin is neither cause why someone is elect to glory or permitted to fall short of it, nor a disposition required for either act, it is improper to say the decree to elect or not elect is prior in God's mind to foresight of sin — and improper to say foresight of sin was prior to that decree — for among independent things there is no before or after in God's mind or will. Those who try to blacken, with I know not what horrid consequences, the view that considers election and passing-by without foresight of sin are twisting ropes out of sand.
source_text: Sed ut paucis expediam quid mei judicii sit hac in re. Primo, si per Praedestinationem quis intelligat solam designationem ad finem gloriae (sicuti multi intelligunt ex antiquioribus Scholasticis) & per Reprobationem solam negationem hujus actus, vel ipsum decretum praetereundi & non-eligendi, puto non esse necessarium ut supponamus peccatum fuisse praevisum in subjecto sic praedestinato aut reprobato, tanquam praecedaneum. Ratio haec est; Quia in actibus mentis & voluntatis Divinae unus non est realiter prior alio, sed tota haec prioritas & posterioritas desumitur ex mutua rerum dependentia: ubi ergo nulla est dependentia causalitatis inter res ipsas, nulla debet aut potest esse consideratio prioritatis aut posterioritatis in decretis Divinis, quae circa easdem versantur. Jam vero peccatum ad actum Divinae electionis vel non-electionis omnino impertinenter se habet: non est enim ratio actus sive hujus sive illius (ut omnes fatentur) neque est talis subjecti qualificatio, absque qua hi actus in subjectum cadere non possunt, sicuti est rationalitas; quod exemplo Angelorum antea demonstratum est. Cum itaque peccatum nec causa sit cur aliquis eligatur ad gloriam, aut permittatur deficere a gloria, nec dispositio subjecti sive ad hunc actum, sive ad illum necessaria, improprie loquitur, qui dicit hoc decretum eligendi aut non eligendi esse prius in mente Divina praevisione peccati; improprie etiam loquitur qui dicit praevisionem peccati fuisse priorem hoc decreto, cum inter res independentes nulla sit ponenda aut prioritas aut posterioritas, sive in mente, sive in voluntate Dei. Atque hinc colligere potestis, illos qui conantur horrendis nescio quibus consequentiis illorum sententiam deturpare, qui considerant decretum electionis & praeteritionis absque praevisione peccati, funiculos ex arena nectere.
